name: רָחָב
summary: Rahab the harlot of Jericho, who hid Joshua's two spies, confessed that “Yahweh your God, he is God in the heavens above and on the earth beneath”, let them down by a cord through her window, and bound the scarlet cord in it; she and her father's house were kept alive when the city was devoted, and she dwelt in Israel (Jos 2:1–21; 6:17–25). The New Testament names her in the line of Jesus Christ as the wife of Salmon and mother of Boaz (Mat 1:5, Ῥαχάβ), among the faithful, “by faith Rahab the harlot did not perish with the disobedient, having received the spies with peace” (Heb 11:31), and as justified by works when she received the messengers and sent them out another way (Jas 2:25); the Peshitta writes רָחָב in all three. The name is spelled as the adjective רָחָב “broad, wide”; scripture does not explain it.

evidence.note: “They came to the house of a harlot, and her name was רָחָב, and lay there.”
“Yahweh your God, he is God in the heavens above and on the earth beneath.”
The scarlet cord bound in the window, and her father's house gathered in.
“Only Rahab the harlot shall live, she and all who are with her in the house, because she hid the messengers.”
Joshua kept her alive, “and she has dwelt in the midst of Israel to this day”.
“By faith Rahab the harlot did not perish with those who did not believe, having received the spies with peace.”
“Was not Rahab the harlot also justified by works, when she received the messengers and sent them out another way?”
The adjective the name is spelled as: “the broad (הָרְחָבָה) and fat land”.

note: TIPNR's Rahab@Job.9.13 is the sea monster רַהַב, another root (רהב), not this name. The adjective's key t.bw.ad also counts these tokens by spelling. Job 30:14 is filed by BDB under the name key too (“as through a wide breach”); it is the adjective. Whether the name is the adjective “broad” or a shortened name (“[the god] has made wide”, like Rehabiah) is not settled; no verse explains it.
